findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 3, Harm 3
Raise: Not done. Case: normal use - another ready pull request lands during this command's tests or CI wait. The requirement is: "When the default branch has moved, a merge retests the combined change first, and it refuses with the names of the failing tests when that retest fails." This condition checks movement before potentially lengthy tests and checks, but nothing refreshes and validates the tested base before merging. Concurrent merges are supported by src/forge/land.py:385–391. Without strict branch protection, which src/forge/init.py:312 leaves disabled by default, GitHub can accept the resulting untested combination. The later retry handles only rejected merges; [--match-head-commit](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr_merge) protects the PR head, not its base. Revalidate the base after testing and waiting, and prevent merging against a different base.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional. Case: normal use - a developer has uncommitted edits in a ready item's worktree. This runs tests directly in that worktree without checking that its files match HEAD. Git can preserve unstaged edits in files untouched by the incoming default-branch change. For example, the added regression's committed left=1/right=1 combination fails, but an unstaged left=0 edit survives the merge and makes the retest pass. The subsequent push publishes HEAD with left=1, and a repository using local tests can merge the failing combination. src/forge/review.py:491–494 executes the command in the supplied worktree; it does not isolate committed contents. Require matching committed contents or test a clean checkout of the head being published.
findings.title: Run the retest against the committed tree that will be pushed

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Functional. Case: normal use - two ready changes edit separate hunks of the same source file and their combined tests pass. This block updates only the local ready receipt after merging and pushing. The committed review still contains its old `changed` fingerprint. src/forge/review.py:158–184 fingerprints the complete blobs of changed files, so the incoming edit changes that fingerprint even for a clean Git merge. The required forge-pr-check then refuses it as out of date at src/forge/prcheck.py:381–382, blocking the green merge until close is run again. Reconcile the committed review through the existing close logic before treating the combined head as ready. The added green test changes separate files, so it misses this case.
findings.title: Refresh the committed review after merging changes to a reviewed file

why: Two items that each passed close merged one after the other and left the default branch red.
